study type: Retrospective population-based study using linked administrative data
exposure: funding source (public patient, private patient, private health insurers, Medicare, individuals)
outcome: cost of maternal and early childhood healthcare
cohort: Women giving birth in Queensland, Australia, whose maternal and early childhood healthcare costs were tracked using a whole-of-population linked administrative dataset.
finding: Private hospital births cost government funders less than public hospital births (an average of $10,050 vs. $21,723), although government funders still contributed approximately 40% of the cost for private hospital births.
mod_finding: Caesarean sections are costly to all funders, and reducing them could lead to significant cost savings, with public hospital funders potentially saving $974 million and private health insurers $216 million.
